from(bucket: "telemetry")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r["_measurement"] == "ai")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r["_field"] == "prediction" or r["_field"] == "est_soh" or r["_field"] == "rul_cycles" or r["_field"] == "cycle" or r["_field"] == "kind")

options.content: Every sensor reading is stored with its timestamp in InfluxDB and in a daily CSV file (data/battery_YYYY-MM-DD.csv). Hover over any chart to see the exact time of each point. Change the time range at the top right to look back further.

Top strip – four answers at a glance: is the ESP32's safety cutoff on, does the twin agree with the pack, what does the AI say, and is data still arriving. Below it, the key live readings.

Digital twin – a Thevenin equivalent-circuit model runs in parallel, fed the same current as the real pack. The residual is the gap between prediction and measurement. A healthy pack tracks its model; a degrading one diverges.

R0 – internal resistance, estimated each time the load changes. Rising R0 is the strongest single indicator of ageing.

Kalman filter – every second it predicts SOC from the current, then corrects it with the measured voltage, learning R0 as it goes. It fixes the drift of coulomb counting and keeps the twin in sync. A sudden R0 rise raises a RESISTANCE JUMP alarm (loose connection or damaged cell).

AI – an XGBoost model estimates state of health from discharge voltage, temperature and cycle count, without a capacity test. SHAP shows which input moved the estimate. Warning = estimate below 85% or projected to reach 80% within 25 cycles; Critical = below 80%.

Tabs – Live pack (this page), AI health demo (an unseen NASA battery replayed through the AI) and What-if simulator (conditions you would never risk on real cells).
